delta.text: # Research Verdict
**Bottom Line:** While benchmark 2018 measurements reported a room-temperature thermal conductivity ($\kappa
$) of ~1300 W/mK for cubic boron arsenide (c-BAs) [4
], the record does not establish 1300 W/mK as a strict intrinsic ceiling; recent high-purity and isotopically enriched syntheses
report room-temperature values reaching ~1500 W/mK [6] to above 210

0 W/mK [5].

### theory predictions
First-principles three-phonon calculations in 2013 initially
predicted room-temperature $\kappa$ exceeding 2000 W/mK [1], though this baseline was
overturned by the human jury in favor of subsequent four-phonon resistance models [2]. Incorporating four-phonon scattering in 2017 revised

the theoretical 300 K prediction downward to 1400 W/mK [3].

### measurement history
In 2018, Kang et al. measured 1300 W/mK in defect-free regions [4], while Li
et al. and Tian et al. reported 1000 $\pm$ 90 W/mK [
7] and 1160 $\pm$ 130 W/mK [8], respectively.
However, post-2020 studies have not strictly converged on 1200–1300 W
/mK [14]; recent defect-minimized crystals have yielded measurements of ~1500 W/

mK [6] and over 2100 W/mK [5].

### material defects
Vacancies and group-IV impurities Incorporate on the As site and strongly suppress lattice thermal conductivity in typical as-grown crystals [9][1
0]. Conversely, first-principles doping models indicate specific $\text{C}_\text{B}$ and $\text{
Ge}_\text{As}$ impurities can retain $\kappa$ above ~1000 W/mK even at high

densities [11].

### method disputes
Time-domain thermoreflectance (TDTR) measurements exhibit heating-size
reductions due to quasi-ballistic phonon transport [12], though experimentalists report modulation-frequency independence when using large (

70 $\mu\text{m}$) pump beams [13].

### applications outlook
Optical transient grating measurements
confirmed simultaneous $\kappa$ of 1200 W/mK and ambipolar mobility of 1600 $\text
{cm}^2/\text{Vs}$ locally [15], though unintentional doping and spatial nonuniformity can degrade bulk
hole mobility to 40 $\text{cm}^2/\text{Vs}$ [16]. Chemical vapor transport

(CVT) growth remains hindered by millimeter-scale size limits and quality control bottlenecks [17].

## Contested & ruled
On claim c
1, the Advocate cited 2013 three-phonon predictions over 2000 W/mK [1], whereas
the Skeptic showed that four-phonon thermal resistance reduces this prediction from 2200 to 1400 W/
mK [2]. *Per human ruling: "b" — "rule for the counter-evidence" (note: "auto-resolved (CLI
)")*. A tie-breaker agent dispatched on c2 confirmed that Feng et al. (2017) explicitly calculated
the four-phonon reduced value at 1400 W/mK [3]. Unruled disputes remain across
c3, c4, c5, c6, c7, and c8 regarding whether post-202
4 syntheses (>1500–2100 W/mK) [5][6] supersede the
2018 benchmarks [4][7] and how severely point defects and ballistic transport skew bulk extraction [9
